title: Indicator Functions in Lp
content: Proves that indicator functions $\mathbf{1}_E$ of finite-measure measurable sets belong to $L^p$ for $1 \leq p < \infty$, with norm $\|\mathbf{1}_E\|_p = \mu(E)^{1/p}$. The proof delegates to `Memℒp.indicator` and `memℒp_const` — indicators are bounded by the constant function 1, which is always in $L^p$. The norm formula follows from $\int |\mathbf{1}_E|^p\,d\mu = \mu(E)$.

title: Absolute Continuity: Indicators of Null Sets Vanish in Lp
content: Two lemmas establishing that indicators of null sets are zero almost everywhere and have zero $L^p$ norm. If $\mu(E) = 0$, then $\mathbf{1}_E = 0$ $\mu$-a.e. because the set where $\mathbf{1}_E \neq 0$ is contained in $E$, which has measure zero. The `eLpNorm_eq_zero_of_ae_zero` lemma then gives $\|\mathbf{1}_E\|_p = 0$. These are the technical prerequisites for the absolute continuity argument in Step 2.

title: Functional-Induced Set Function and AC Condition
content:
The core construction: given $\varphi \in (L^p)^*$, define $
u(E) = \varphi(\mathbf{1}_E)$ for measurable sets $E$ with $\mu(E) < \infty$. The key theorem `functionalSetFn_null` proves absolute continuity: if $\mu(E) = 0$, then $\mathbf{1}_E = 0$ in $L^p$, so $
u(E) = \varphi(0) = 0$. This uses `map_zero` after showing the $L^p$ representative is the zero function. The absolute continuity $
u \ll \mu$ is what enables the Radon-Nikodym step.

title: Radon-Nikodym Reconstruction
content: Applies Mathlib's Radon-Nikodym theorem: for a signed measure $s$ absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$, the RN derivative $g = ds/d\mu$ reconstructs $s$ via $\mu.\mathrm{withDensity}_v(g) = s$. This is a direct application of `SignedMeasure.absolutelyContinuous_iff_withDensityᵥ_rnDeriv_eq`, one of Mathlib's most substantial measure theory results. The RN derivative is the candidate representing function for the Riesz theorem.

title: Holder Extremizer Argument (Infrastructure Gap)
content: Documents the key infrastructure gap: showing $g \in L^q$ via the Holder extremizer trick. The classical proof (Rudin 6.16) takes the test function $s = |g|^{q/p} \cdot \mathrm{sgn}(g)$, which is the unique function achieving equality in Holder's inequality. Substituting into $|\varphi(s)| \leq \|\varphi\| \cdot \|s\|_p$ gives $\int |g|^q \, d\mu \leq \|\varphi\|^q$, hence $\|g\|_q \leq \|\varphi\|$. This requires measurability of $|g|^{q/p} \cdot \mathrm{sgn}(g)$, its $L^p$ membership, and the norm computation — each nontrivial in Lean.

title: Integral Representation via Density
content: States the extension of $\varphi(f) = \int fg\,d\mu$ from indicators to all of $L^p$. The argument: (1) the identity holds on indicators $\mathbf{1}_E$ by construction; (2) by linearity, it extends to simple functions; (3) simple functions are dense in $L^p$ (Mathlib's `Lp.simpleFunc.denseRange`); (4) both sides are continuous in $f$ (the LHS by $\varphi$ being bounded, the RHS by Holder's inequality), so they agree on all of $L^p$.
mathContext: $\varphi(\mathbf{1}_E) = \int_E g\,d\mu$ for all $E$ $\implies$ $\varphi(f) = \int fg\,d\mu$ for all $f \in L^p$

title: Riesz Representation Surjectivity (Main Theorem)
content: The main theorem: every bounded linear functional $\varphi \in (L^p)^*$ is represented by integration against some $g \in L^q$, i.e., $\varphi(f) = \int fg\,d\mu$ for all $f \in L^p$, where $1/p + 1/q = 1$ and $1 < p < \infty$. This is the surjectivity half of the Riesz representation theorem for $L^p$ spaces. Combined with the embedding $(L^q \hookrightarrow (L^p)^*)$ from Holder's inequality, it establishes the isometric isomorphism $(L^p)^* \cong L^q$.
mathContext: $\forall \varphi \in (L^p)^*, \exists g \in L^q : \varphi(f) = \int fg\,d\mu$ for all $f \in L^p$ ($1 < p < \infty$, $1/p + 1/q = 1$)

title: Assessment: Axiom Eliminability
content: Summarizes the status: the parent file's `riesz_lp_surjective` axiom IS eliminable using Mathlib's infrastructure. Steps 1-3 (indicators in $L^p$, absolute continuity, Radon-Nikodym) are proved from Mathlib. Steps 4-5 (Holder extremizer for $L^q$ membership, density extension) require approximately 200 lines of formalization but face no mathematical obstacles — all required Mathlib primitives exist. Notably, Aristotle cannot help because these are infrastructure composition tasks, not single-lemma proofs.
mathContext: 3 of 5 proof steps formalized; 2 remain (~200 lines of infrastructure, no mathematical gaps)
